name: Haziel
overview: Haziel is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified as the son of Shimei within the family of Ladan. His mention is brief and specific, highlighting his genealogical placement among the Levites, a tribe set apart for priestly duties. There are no additional notes or details about his life or role beyond this lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Haziel means 'vision of God [El],' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's presence or revelation. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:9, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries spiritual significance through its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Haziel is the son of Shimei, situating him within the Levitical family of Ladan. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Haziel's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role within the tribe of Levi, particularly as part of the family of Ladan. This lineage is important for understanding the organization and division of Levitical duties in Israel. While the biblical record does not elaborate on his personal actions or contributions, his inclusion affirms the continuity of Levitical families entrusted with sacred responsibilities.
